sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Kettlebell Hip Thrust is a glute-focused hip extension exercise where the lifter rests their upper back on a bench and drives their hips up while a kettlebell is held over the hips for resistance.

It is a convenient loaded variation of the hip thrust for lifters who only have a kettlebell available, or as an accessory exercise alongside heavier barbell hip thrust work.

The movement produces a strong glute contraction and is suitable for beginners through advanced lifters.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Targets the glutes through direct hip extension loading
- Excellent option when no barbell is available
- Easy to scale load with different kettlebell weights
- Reinforces strong hip extension mechanics
- Builds glute size, strength, and endurance
- Supports better performance in compound lower body lifts
- Can be progressed with tempo, pauses, or single leg variations

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Gluteus Maximus

Secondary: Hamstrings, Core, Erector Spinae, Quadriceps

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Sit on the ground with your back against a bench, knees bent.
2. Place your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
3. Place a kettlebell over your hips, holding it securely with both hands by the handle.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Position your shoulder blades against the bench.
2. When you thrust upwards, your body should form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees at the top of the movement.
3. Brace your core and grip the kettlebell handle to keep it stable.

sections.heading: Lift
sections.content:
1. Brace your core and drive through your heels.
2. Lift your hips and the kettlebell upwards until your hips are fully extended.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement for maximum engagement.

sections.heading: Lower and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Lower your hips back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
2. Keep tension in your glutes throughout the movement.
3. Ensure the kettlebell remains securely positioned on your hips. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Hyper-extending the lower back at the top
- Letting the kettlebell shift up the abdomen
- Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
- Letting the knees cave inward
- Failing to fully extend the hips
- Tucking the chin too aggressively or letting the head drop
- Holding the breath through the rep

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Kettlebell of appropriate weight
- Stable bench or sturdy elevated surface
- Athletic shoes for foot traction
- Optional: Pad or towel for hip comfort
- Optional: Mat for floor comfort

sections.heading: Kettlebell Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Use a pad or folded towel under the kettlebell to protect the hips.
2. Keep both hands firmly on the kettlebell handle throughout the rep.
3. Place the bench against a wall to prevent it from sliding.
4. Choose a load that allows controlled reps with full hip extension.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
2. Torso: Shoulder blades on the bench, ribs stacked, core braced.
3. Knees: Bent at roughly 90 degrees in the top position.
4. Hips: Driven up to full extension, glutes squeezed.
5. Head: Neutral, chin slightly tucked, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Hip Thrust: Heavier loaded version
- Dumbbell Hip Thrust: Loaded with a dumbbell
- Bodyweight Hip Thrust: Unloaded learning variation
- Glute Bridge: Floor-based hip extension
- Single Leg Hip Thrust: Unilateral variation
- Standing Hip Thrust Machine: Machine-based hip extension

sections.heading: Kettlebell Hip Thrust Variations
sections.content:
Standard Kettlebell Hip Thrust: Described here
Single Leg Kettlebell Hip Thrust: One leg lifted for unilateral demand
Feet Elevated Kettlebell Hip Thrust: Feet on a step or box for greater stretch
B Stance Kettlebell Hip Thrust: One foot lightly placed for unilateral bias
Paused Kettlebell Hip Thrust: Pause at the top for greater glute tension
Tempo Kettlebell Hip Thrust: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Lower Back Pain: Avoid over-extending at the top, focus on glute squeeze
Knee Pain: Adjust foot position to reduce knee strain
No Bench: Perform a glute bridge on the floor instead
Shoulder Discomfort: Use a padded bench edge or towel for the upper back
Hip Discomfort: Use a folded towel under the kettlebell
Beginners: Start with bodyweight hip thrusts before adding load
